newsitem.title: USA: World Food Prize winner says India can feed itself.
newsitem.headline: World Food Prize winner says India can feed itself.

text.p: India should be able to feed itself for years into the future if the proper investments are made in agriculture, the co-winner of the World Food Prize, Gurdev Singh Khush, said on Tuesday.
"I have no reason to believe we cannot feed our people" for the next 30 or 40 years, Khush said at a news conference.
Khush, 61, was born in India and has been principal plant breeder at the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines since 1972.
Henry Beachell, his predecessor at IRRI, and Khush were co-winners of the $200,000 prize for their development of widely used rice varieties.
Rice yields in India were comparatively low, averaging about three metric tons per hectare, so there was plenty of room for improvement, Khush said.
With proper amounts of fertiliser, water and cultivation, yields could double, he said. Improved roads and marketing systems would spur farmers to grow more.
India blossomed into the unusual position of being one of the world's leading rice exporters last year.
"That's temporary," Khush said, saying domestic demand was certain to catch up with output.
